gap: No result ChatGPT got states an independently measured capacity for any lithium trolling-motor battery. Techtest.org measured 102–103 Ah from LiTime's 12V 100Ah trolling-motor battery with low-temperature protection across five discharges at 10–40 A, and Panbo measured 101.75 Ah from WattCycle's 12V 100Ah trolling-motor battery. No named reviewer has published a capacity figure for the premium Dakota, Battle Born or Ionic 12V 100Ah.
standout_why: I opened Outdoor Life (Pete Robbins, updated 2024-06-10), Boating Mag (Elliott Stark, updated 2026-07-28), Minormania's lithium trolling-motor list and Ionic's trolling-motor category page, which ChatGPT cited. All of them give only maker specs, owner anecdotes or survey runtimes. Minormania attributes an unnamed '278-279Ah' figure to 'independent capacity tests' for an ECO-WORTHY 280Ah. None names who measured what, and none has a measured Ah figure for any 12V 100Ah candidate. Wired2Fish, which ChatGPT cited, returned HTTP 403, and Dakota's cited category page returned HTTP 429, so I could not check those two.
decides: It backs ChatGPT's 'best value' pick, the LiTime 12V 100Ah TM. A named lab measured 2–3% above rated capacity at trolling-motor currents up to 40 A, with ~90% of the energy delivered between 13.2 V and 12.6 V. ChatGPT's premium picks (Dakota $795, Battle Born $849, Ionic $649) have no published independent capacity measurement. Their higher price rests on warranty and brand, not on any measured capacity edge. One caveat for cold-weather buyers: Panbo found that LiTime's non-TM 12V 200Ah would still charge with its sensor well below 0 °F. That makes the TM model's low-temperature cutoff the feature to check.

findings.product: LiTime 12V 100Ah LiFePO4 trolling-motor battery with low-temperature protection
findings.label: Measured capacity
findings.source_title: Der LiTime 12V 100Ah LiFePO4 Akku für Trolling Motoren mit Tieftemperaturschutz im Test (Techtest.org, Michael Barton, 2023-12-22)
findings.note: Five charge/discharge cycles: three at 10 A, one at 20 A and one at 40 A. 102-103 Ah is 2–3% over rating. The article gives no Wh figure; 1280 Wh is the maker spec.

findings.product: LiTime 12V 100Ah LiFePO4 trolling-motor battery with low-temperature protection
findings.label: Measured BMS low-voltage cutoff and voltage curve
findings.value: Shut off at 10.43 V; ~90% of capacity delivered between 13.2 V and 12.6 V
findings.source_title: Der LiTime 12V 100Ah LiFePO4 Akku für Trolling Motoren mit Tieftemperaturschutz im Test (Techtest.org, Michael Barton, 2023-12-22)
findings.note: About 13.6 V when full, dropping to about 13.2 V within 10 minutes at 10 A. The voltage falls fast below 12.6 V. Barton treats 12.5 V and below as empty. The low-temperature charge cutoff threshold was not measured.

findings.label: Measured capacity and high-current shutdown
findings.value: About 101.75 Ah measured; shut down only at almost 200 A (rated 120 A continuous)
findings.source_title: WattCycle LiFePO4, value battery with a punch (Panbo, Ben Stein, 2024-12-11, updated 2025-01-12)
findings.note: The article gives no discharge current for the capacity test. Panbo lists the price at $219 (this is not today's store price). Stein calls the result 'slightly under the 2-3 percent margin over rated capacity I typically see.'

findings.label: Measured capacity, sustained current and cold-charge behaviour
findings.value: 202.4 Ah at 10 A; sustained 150 A; FET temperature shutdown after about 3 min at 175 A; no low-temperature charge cutoff (still charged with the probe well below 0 °F)
findings.source_title: Li Time LiFePO4, no frills, serious value (Panbo, Ben Stein, 2023-03-10)
findings.note: This is a different model from the TM battery and is listed only for brand context. At 95 A the hottest FET stabilised at 155–156 °F, and the BMS disconnected at about 250 °F. It shows why trolling-motor buyers in cold areas should choose the TM version with a low-temperature cutoff.

findings.label: Measured capacity at three currents
findings.source_title: Test: Redodo 12 V 100 Ah LiFePO4, wirklich 100Ah Kapazität? (ja) (Techtest.org, Michael Barton, 2022-08-16)
findings.note: Charged with a 14.6 V charger and discharged to below 11 V. This is not the Redodo trolling-motor (Group 31, low-temp cutoff) model Dealectric lists, so it is brand context only.

findings.label: Thermal reading under load
findings.value: 133 degrees (unit not stated) during a 150 A continuous discharge
findings.source_title: My test bench runneth over with lithium from SFK, Mastervolt, and Epoch (Panbo, Ben Stein, 2024-08-22)
findings.note: Measured with a thermal camera; Stein reads it as the battery 'isn't working too hard.' Epoch rates it at 150 A continuous and 800 A for 10 s. The article reports no measured Ah.
